how: Around your ribcage, just under the bust, snug: that's close to your band.
Around the fullest part, loose: the difference between the two is the start of your cup.
Then forget both numbers and come in. Shapes fit differently; our fitters fit the bra, not the tape.

problems.label: The band rides up at the back
problems.means: Usually the band is too big, so the straps are doing the work instead.
problems.ask: Can I try a smaller band and a cup up?

problems.label: The cup gaps at the top
problems.means: Often the shape, not the size: a full cup on a shallow bust leaves space.
problems.ask: Which of your shapes suit a shallower bust?

problems.label: I spill over the cup
problems.means: Usually the cup is too small, or the cut is too low for you.
problems.ask: Can we try a cup up, or a fuller cut?

problems.label: The straps dig in
problems.means: The band may be too loose, leaving the straps to hold everything.
problems.ask: Is my band doing its job?

problems.label: The wire sits on my breast
problems.means: Usually the cup is too small, or the wire is the wrong width for you.
problems.ask: Can you check the wire width?

sections.title: What happens
sections.text:
We ask what you wear and what it does. We measure once, then put the tape away and fit you in the shapes that suit you.
Most of the fitting is trying on. You leave with your sizes written down, whether you buy or not.

photo.alt: A smoke lace bralette worn against white fur

sections.title: How it should fit
sections.text: The band level all the way round, firm enough to hold on its own. The centre flat against you. The cup smooth, no gap, no spill. The straps resting, not working.

care.title: Cold water. *A little patience.*
care.intro: Lace and silk last for years if you let them.
care.description: How to wash and keep lace and silk lingerie, from Marese.

opener.alt: Ivory silk satin gathered on black

sections.title: Lace
sections.text: By hand, in cool water, with a little gentle wash. Press the water out in a towel; never wring. Dry flat, away from heat.

sections.title: Silk
sections.text: By hand or on a silk cycle, in a bag. Iron inside out, on low, while still a little damp.

sections.title: Leavers lace
sections.text: Leavers lace is woven slowly on machines built for it, the threads twisted rather than knitted, which is why the edge holds its scallop. Ours is cut by hand to follow the pattern, so no two pieces fall on quite the same flower.

questions.q: Is a fitting free? Do I have to buy?
questions.a: Free, forty-five minutes, and no, you don't. You leave with your sizes written down either way.

questions.q: Can I bring my partner, or my mother?
questions.a: One guest, yes. Or come alone; most do.
Yes: the private evening. The salon closes for you, one fitter, ninety minutes. See the free evenings on the home page.

questions.q: I'm buying for her. What if I don't know her size?
questions.a: Tell us what you know and we'll choose with you, or start with a robe or a camisole. She can exchange anything unworn for her size within 28 days (demo policy).

questions.q: Is the packaging discreet? What shows on the statement?
questions.a: Posted, it travels in a plain brown box. On a bank statement it reads MARESE LTD (demo).

From the salon, our policy decides: unworn pieces with their hygiene strip in place can be exchanged within 28 days (demo policy). Bought online or by phone, you have 14 days to cancel, except sealed items, such as briefs, once their seal is broken after delivery. Anything faulty, always.

questions.q: How early should I come for bridal?
questions.a: Three months before your final dress fitting. Bring the dress, or photographs of its back and neckline.
The salon is on the first floor, up one flight of stairs. If stairs are difficult, tell us and we'll fit you on the ground floor.
